stem: If $\sin {=a}x^\circ=\cos {=b}x^\circ$, where ${=a}x^\circ$ and ${=b}x^\circ$ are acute angles, find the value of $x$.
solution: The sine of an angle equals the cosine of its complementary angle.
Check: ${=a}x={=a * x}^\circ$ and ${=b}x={=b * x}^\circ$, which add up to 90°.
notes: Complementary-angle rule sin θ = cos(90° − θ). x = 90/s always whole; both angles acute.
